root_cause.text: In the Tegra194 PCIe endpoint reset-deassert path, cleanup/deinit was invoked in the wrong order so functions reached DesignWare DBI register accesses before `reset_control_deassert(pcie->core_rst)` powered on the controller core.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly shows `pci_epc_deinit_notify()` → `dw_pcie_ep_clear_bar()` → `__dw_pcie_ep_reset_bar()` → `dw_pcie_dbi_ro_wr_en()` accessing DBI offset `0x8bc` before `reset_control_deassert(pcie->core_rst)`, and the patch fixes it by moving `pci_epc_deinit_notify()` and `dw_pcie_ep_cleanup()` to after the core reset deassert.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop performing endpoint deinitialization and cleanup during PCIe reset deassert handling so the endpoint is not incorrectly torn down at re-enable time.
intent_record.what: Two cleanup calls, pci_epc_deinit_notify(pcie->pci.ep.epc) and dw_pcie_ep_cleanup(&pcie->pci.ep), along with their preceding comment about refclk-dependent cleanup, were removed from pex_ep_event_pex_rst_deassert() after the PHY/power-up handling and before clearing interrupt status registers.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the deassert-reset path no longer performs endpoint deinitialization and DesignWare endpoint cleanup at that point, so the endpoint state is preserved instead of being torn down during reset deassert handling, avoiding unnecessary or incorrect cleanup during reinitialization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Run endpoint deinit notification and DesignWare endpoint cleanup after core reset deassert so reset-time cleanup occurs in the required hardware state.
intent_record.what: Two function calls, pci_epc_deinit_notify(pcie->pci.ep.epc) and dw_pcie_ep_cleanup(&pcie->pci.ep), were added immediately after reset_control_deassert(pcie->core_rst) in pex_ep_event_pex_rst_deassert(), along with a comment stating that this cleanup requires refclk and core reset to be deasserted.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when PCIe reset is deasserted for the endpoint, the code now explicitly notifies EPC deinitialization and performs DesignWare endpoint cleanup only after the reference clock and core reset are active, ensuring teardown steps run in a valid hardware state and avoiding missed or improperly timed cleanup.

grouping_result.intent: Run endpoint deinit notification and DesignWare endpoint cleanup after core reset deassert so reset-time cleanup occurs in the required hardware state.

consistency_review.core_intent: Move endpoint deinitialization and DesignWare endpoint cleanup to occur after PCIe core reset deassert so reset-time teardown happens in the correct hardware state.
consistency_review.reason: Hunk 1 matches the core intent by adding the cleanup after reset deassert, but Hunk 0 is framed as stopping deinitialization/cleanup during reset deassert handling, which conflicts with that purpose rather than describing the same move.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it reorders endpoint deinit/cleanup to occur after core reset deassert, preventing DesignWare DBI accesses before the controller core is powered on.

The root cause is incorrect reset-deassert sequencing that performs teardown/cleanup before the controller core is powered on, leading to premature DBI access. This group directly removes endpoint deinitialization/cleanup from reset deassert handling, addressing that wrong-order teardown behavior.

candidates.rationale: This cleanup reaches DesignWare endpoint/DBI register accesses, and in the pre-fix ordering it was invoked before core reset deassert, directly matching the root cause.
This deinit notification was part of the wrongly ordered reset-deassert cleanup sequence; it was explicitly moved/removed so teardown would not occur before the controller core was powered on.

vuln_statements.explanation: This cleanup call was executed in the reset-deassert path before the controller core reset was deasserted. It can reach DesignWare endpoint/DBI register accesses while the core is still powered off, which matches the root cause.

This deinitialization notification was part of the incorrect teardown sequence during reset deassert. It contributed to invoking endpoint deinit/cleanup before core power-up via reset deassert, enabling the unsafe path to DBI register access.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the exact reset-assert and reset-deassert ordering relevant to the root cause. In `pex_ep_event_pex_rst_assert()`, the vulnerable cleanup calls were removed: `pci_epc_deinit_notify(pcie->pci.ep.epc);` and `dw_pcie_ep_cleanup(&pcie->pci.ep);` are deleted before `reset_control_assert(pcie->core_rst);`.
